passages.text: Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient and ready for every good work, to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Titus and the believers in Crete.
Paul tells Titus to remind the believers about their duties.
Believers must submit to rulers and authorities.
Believers must obey those in authority.
Believers must be ready to do every good work.
Believers must not speak evil of anyone.
Believers must not quarrel.
Believers must be gentle.
Believers must show true humility to everyone.
passages.original: Ὑπομίμνῃσκε αὐτοὺς ἀρχαῖς ἐξουσίαις ὑποτάσσεσθαι πειθαρχεῖν πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἑτοίμους εἶναι μηδένα βλασφημεῖν ἀμάχους εἶναι ἐπιεικεῖς πᾶσαν ἐνδεικνυμένους πραΰτητα πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους

passages.text: For at one time we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, and enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures—living in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.
passages.sermon:
We were once foolish people.
We did not obey God.
We went astray.
We served many desires and pleasures.
We lived in malice.
We lived in envy.
People hated us.
We hated each other.
passages.original: Ἦμεν γάρ ποτε καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀνόητοι ἀπειθεῖς πλανώμενοι δουλεύοντες ἐπιθυμίαις καὶ ἡδοναῖς ποικίλαις ἐν κακίᾳ καὶ φθόνῳ διάγοντες στυγητοί μισοῦντες ἀλλήλους

passages.text: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared, He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
God is our Savior.
God is kind.
God loves all people.
God showed His kindness and love to us.
God saved us.
God did not save us because of any good things we had done.
We did not earn our salvation by our own righteous deeds.
God saved us because He is merciful.
God saved us through the washing that brings new birth.
God saved us through the renewal given by the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἡ χρηστότης καὶ ἡ φιλανθρωπία ἐπεφάνη τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων τῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἔσωσεν ἡμᾶς διὰ λουτροῦ παλινγενεσίας καὶ ἀνακαινώσεως Πνεύματος Ἁγίου

passages.text: This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior, so that, having been justified by His grace, we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life.
passages.sermon:
God is our Savior.
God poured out the Holy Spirit on us.
God gave the Holy Spirit to us abundantly.
God did this through Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is our Savior.
God justified us by His grace.
God made us heirs.
God gave us the hope of eternal life.
passages.original: οὗ ἐξέχεεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς πλουσίως διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἵνα δικαιωθέντες τῇ ἐκείνου χάριτι κληρονόμοι γενηθῶμεν κατ’ ἐλπίδα ζωῆς αἰωνίου

passages.text: This saying is trustworthy. And I want you to emphasize these things, so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are excellent and profitable for the people.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to Titus.
Paul was a servant of God.
Paul taught the church in Crete.
Paul said, “This saying is trustworthy.”
Paul wanted Titus to speak clearly about these things.
Paul wanted believers in God to listen.
Believers in God must take care to do good deeds.
Good deeds are excellent.
Good deeds are profitable for people.
passages.original: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ περὶ τούτων βούλομαί σε διαβεβαιοῦσθαι ἵνα φροντίζωσιν καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι οἱ πεπιστευκότες Θεῷ ταῦτά ἐστιν καλὰ καὶ ὠφέλιμα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.
passages.sermon:
Avoid foolish controversies.
Avoid discussions about genealogies.
Avoid arguments.
Avoid quarrels about the law.
These things are pointless.
These things are worthless.
passages.original: Μωρὰς δὲ ζητήσεις καὶ γενεαλογίας καὶ ἔρεις καὶ μάχας νομικὰς περιΐστασο εἰσὶν γὰρ ἀνωφελεῖς καὶ μάταιοι

passages.text: Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition, knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned.
passages.sermon:
A divisive person causes division among believers.
Give a divisive person one warning.
Give a divisive person a second warning.
After these two warnings, reject that person.
Know that this person has turned away from what is right.
This person is sinning.
This person condemns himself.
passages.original: αἱρετικὸν ἄνθρωπον μετὰ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν νουθεσίαν παραιτοῦ εἰδὼς ὅτι ἐξέστραπται ὁ τοιοῦτος καὶ ἁμαρτάνει ὢν αὐτοκατάκριτος

passages.text: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Titus.
Paul plans to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus.
Paul tells Titus to come to him at Nicopolis as soon as Artemas or Tychicus arrives.
Paul has decided to spend the winter in Nicopolis.
passages.original: Ὅταν πέμψω Ἀρτεμᾶν πρὸς σὲ ἢ Τυχικόν σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με εἰς Νικόπολιν ἐκεῖ γὰρ κέκρικα παραχειμάσαι

passages.text: Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.
passages.sermon:
Zenas is a lawyer.
Apollos is a Christian worker.
Help Zenas and Apollos as much as you can.
Make sure Zenas and Apollos have everything they need.
Do not let them lack anything.
passages.original: Ζηνᾶν τὸν νομικὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν σπουδαίως πρόπεμψον ἵνα μηδὲν αὐτοῖς λείπῃ

passages.text: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.
passages.sermon:
Our people must learn something important.
They must learn to do good works.
They must lead in doing what is good.
They must help with urgent needs.
They must meet the needs of others.
If they do this, they will not be unfruitful.
passages.original: μανθανέτωσαν δὲ καὶ οἱ ἡμέτεροι καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι εἰς τὰς ἀναγκαίας χρείας ἵνα μὴ ὦσιν ἄκαρποι

passages.text: All who are with me send you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with all of you.
passages.sermon: All the people with me send you greetings.\r\nGreet everyone who loves us in the faith.\r\nMay God’s grace be with all of you.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζονταί σε οἱ μετ’ ἐμοῦ πάντες Ἄσπασαι τοὺς φιλοῦντας ἡμᾶς ἐν πίστει Ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν
